name: JellyMesh
overview: Federates multiple Jellyfin servers into one library
description: JellyMesh shows films and series from other Jellyfin servers in your existing libraries and streams them through the local server. Duplicates become one title: a local copy always wins, otherwise the best quality does, and the other copies stay as backups. Remote servers can be stock Jellyfin or run JellyMesh, which adds shared libraries, stream limits and a change feed between servers you trust. An admin can merge films that can't be matched safely.

versions.changelog:
- The plugin records which server last served each federated title to each user, ready for the per-server folders of 0.5.
- Another user can no longer stop, restart or keep alive a federated title you play through this server's own transcode by naming its play session, even during a long pause or after the title is renamed or removed.
- Start, progress and ping reports of another user on that play session are answered without effect.
- Another user can no longer stop that transcode with a request that names your device and no play session.
- Each user keeps at most 256 of these play sessions; beyond that the least recently used one leaves first.

Not verified: a long pause on a real client, and the record of the last server across a plugin upgrade.

- Stock streaming, subtitle, attachment and trickplay requests check the federated title they name, also as the version picked with mediaSourceId, videoId or the legacy params: without a signed-in user they get 401, and a user who cannot see the title gets 404.
- A stock stream can no longer reuse the play session of a federated title to reach it from another title.
- An anonymous attachment request no longer makes the server refresh a federated title.
- The page no longer warns about a library that holds the federated folder together with other folders: it counts as linked.
- The README explains that a user connected as a server cannot use that server from an app or the web client.

Not verified: a play session reused from another title is covered by unit tests only, not on a running server.

The credential key now lives in a file the plugin creates in its data folder, so JELLYMESH_SECRET_KEY is no longer needed: credentials saved with it move to the file once at startup. If saved passwords can no longer be read, the page asks for them again on each server. On Windows the key file gets an explicit access list (the account running Jellyfin, SYSTEM, Administrators); this is not yet tried on a Windows server. Only removing a server from the page deletes its content, so an emptied settings file no longer wipes the federated folder; the Catalog tab offers to forget servers missing from the settings. A server whose removal cannot be saved stays configured, and a removed server's copies leave the manual merges. Films that a remote groups into collections now reach the library, large catalogs materialize much faster, and sync reads retry brief remote errors. The .strm endpoint refuses requests that come through a proxy; the README covers the reverse proxy case.

Redesigns the plugin page around the JellyMesh identity, in a dark and a light scheme that follow the Jellyfin theme, and shows it in English or Italian according to the language set in Jellyfin. After connecting a server, the page goes straight to choosing its libraries. Removing a server now deletes its content right away, while titles also on another server stay and move to it. The first setup step says what to do about the secret key. Remote playback is checked only on 12.4, with jellyfin-web only: real Android and TV clients and QSV are not yet tested.

Adds a logo, shown in the plugin catalog, and a JellyMesh entry in the Plugins section of the Dashboard menu. The federated folder can now be set with the JELLYMESH_FEDERATED_ROOT environment variable, which then wins over the plugin page. The logo and the menu entry are checked on Jellyfin 12.0 and 12.4, and remote playback only on 12.4, with jellyfin-web only: real Android and TV clients and QSV are not yet tested.

Loads on every Jellyfin 12.x. Earlier versions were built against the 12.4 packages, so older 12.x servers installed them and then showed them as NotSupported. The plugin page is checked on Jellyfin 12.2 and 12.4, and remote playback only on 12.4, with jellyfin-web only: real Android and TV clients and QSV are not yet tested.

A redesigned plugin page, split into five tabs and built from Jellyfin's own controls. It adds a health summary, first-run steps and status cards for servers, says how each action ended and what a removal will do, and picks the federated folder in Jellyfin's folder browser. Doubtful films now show the quality of each copy and what a merge would play. Tested on Jellyfin 12.4 with jellyfin-web only: real Android and TV clients and QSV are not yet tested.

First release, for Jellyfin 12.x. Films and series from stock and JellyMesh remotes, with dedup and per-episode completion, written to a federated folder you link to your libraries. Remote playback through the local server, with backup sources and a local transcode as fallback. Shared libraries and stream limits between JellyMesh servers, and manual film merges. Tested on Jellyfin 12.4 with jellyfin-web only: real Android and TV clients and QSV are not yet tested.
